description: A pooled analysis of items treats each examination item as its own comparison: correct-answer rates are computed per item with 95% confidence intervals and combined in a random-effects proportional meta-analysis yielding a school-level odds ratio.
title: Pooled analysis of items

description: The article articulates an epistemic framework contrasting two measurement traditions.
title: Population-first versus individual-first measurement framework

description: The article's central recommendation: with large-scale assessment data, 'inferences are only possible at the population-level—and then only when framed as conditional on the assessment design and assumptions—not at the level of individual students'.
title: Population-level inference with plausible values conditional on assessment design

description: The article argues that portable EEG provides an objective, real-time index of classroom attention that behavioral observation and self-report cannot supply, because those methods \"are each indirect and cannot pick up the dynamic changes in student engagement\".
title: Portable classroom EEG for continuous attention measurement

description: The article built a comparative evaluation testbed simulating an institution's position under vendor procurement: a research replica EWS and six post-hoc fairness methods applied without accessing, modifying, or retraining the underlying model.
title: Post-hoc fairness evaluation testbed for vendor-controlled early-warning systems

title: Post-processing pipeline for motion-capture measurement data in surgical skill evaluation

description: A model that rates each school's effectiveness by regressing average school test scores on school poverty level and standardizing the residuals.
title: Poverty-adjusted value-added school effectiveness rating model

title: Power analysis framework for cross-level mediation in three-level cluster-randomized trials

description: The article's design recommendation for efficacy trials aiming at moderator questions: because the total number of individuals, not clusters, drives power for individual-level moderators, planners should increase students per cluster.
title: Power planning for individual-level moderators in cluster-randomized education trials

description: Because the article develops power formulas specifically for exploratory analyses linking teacher practice outcomes to student achievement outcomes in clustered school-based RCTs, it implies that researchers should evaluate power for these analyses when designing studies.
title: Power planning for mediator–outcome linkage analyses in clustered education RCTs
